# Choose membership and network resources

SpaMTP uses identifiers and pathway memberships from a versioned snapshot of
the RaMP database, and archived topology from
[graphite](https://bioconductor.org/packages/graphite/). The Bioconductor data
package SpaMTPdb distributes these snapshots with checksums. Memberships
define enrichment and score calculations; network edges supply interaction
context for displaying those results. This guide connects the analysis and
plotting interfaces, explains how to explore the worked human RNA/MSI network,
and inspects the KEGG Cell Cycle interaction records and their provenance.

| Resource | Contents and use |
|:--|:--|
| `source_df`, `analyte` | Resolve measured identifiers to RaMP entities |
| `pathway`, `analytehaspathway` | Build pathway memberships and measured universes |
| `chem_props` | Chemical properties for mass-based annotation |
| `ramp_kegg` | Human Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) interactions |
| `ramp_reactome` | Human Reactome interactions |
| `ramp_wikipathway` | Human WikiPathways interactions |
| `ramp_hmdb` | Human Small Molecule Pathway Database (SMPDB) interactions, under the historical SpaMTP resource name |

Load the collections needed for your analysis. The [joint-pathway guide](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways)
uses memberships for measured genes and metabolites. The
[annotation guide](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#carry-the-annotation-threshold-into-real-pathway-analysis)
shows how scored compound identities enter a network.

## Snapshot versions and interpretation

RaMP 3.0.7 memberships and graphite archive-19 topology (2022-11-01) have separate
provenance. Source-specific pathway IDs and memberships are retained during
identifier reconciliation. Membership coverage counts the measured pathway
members; topology coverage records the available interactions between nodes.
`pathwayNetworkPlots()` accepts pathway names or source IDs, but its exported
views are keyed by pathway name. Filter to one database when names recur
across sources.

# Choose an analysis and its display

Choose the display for your question. The linked examples share the same
`pathwayIndex` for identifier mapping and memberships.

| Question | Analysis and display | Worked example |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Are selected genes overrepresented in pathways? | `fishersPathwayAnalysis()` with an explicit measured universe | [Foreground and universe](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#foreground-and-measured-universe) |
| Which pathways have positive or negative regional ranks? | `findRegionalPathways()`, then `plotRegionalPathways()` | [Joint regional effects](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#regional-pathway-plot) |
| Where does measured pathway expression vary? | `createPathwayObject()`, `plotPathwaysSpatially()` | [Pathway assays and spatial plots](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#pathway-assays-and-spatial-plots) |
| How do measured members relate to known interactions? | `pathwayNetworkPlots()`, then `embedPathwayNetwork()` | [Interactive RNA/MSI network](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#pathway-network) |
| Which gene sets co-vary across locations? | `runRAMPGeseca()` | [RNA co-regulation](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#pathway-coregulation) |

`createPathwayAssay()` creates **identity-level** gene or compound rows;
`createPathwayObject()` creates **pathway-level** scores.

## Enrichment of measured glioma RNA markers

The bundled human glioma example contains 240 aligned tissue locations and
a 339-gene Xenium panel. This example selects positive markers for the
archived `Oligo` group and tests their pathway memberships against the measured
RNA panel. The [gene-mapping guide](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#demonstration-data-and-pinned-inputs)
describes the tissue data and its source.

Load RaMP 3.0.7 memberships and the HGNC reference, then resolve the measured
gene names. `measured_genes` supplies the mapped background for enrichment.

```{r membership-data, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
library(SpatialExperiment)
database <- loadSpaMTPDatabase(
    c("source_df", "analyte", "analytehaspathway", "pathway"),
    version = "3.0.7"
)
reference <- SpaMTPdb::spaMTPdbGeneReference(version = "2026.7.7")
gene_index <- buildGeneMappingIndex(database$source_df, geneReference = reference)
pathway_index <- buildPathwayIndex(database, geneIndex = gene_index)
spe <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "human_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
rna <- altExp(spe, "SPT")
gene_mapping <- mapGeneIdentifiers(rownames(rna), index = gene_index)
measured_genes <- gene_mapping$input[gene_mapping$status == "mapped"]
table(gene_mapping$status)
```

Normalize RNA counts, rank the positive `Oligo` markers by mean AUC, and
select the first 20 mapped genes. `minPathSize = 5` selects pathways with at
least five members in the mapped panel.

```{r membership-enrichment, message=FALSE}
spe <- normalizeSMData(spe, "LogNormalize", assay = "SPT", verbose = FALSE)
markers <- findAllDEMs(spe,
    ident = "cout_labels", assay = "SPT", assayName = "logcounts",
    method = "markers", spatialBlocks = 0, verbose = FALSE
)
foreground <- subset(markers$DEMs,
    cluster == "Oligo" & logFC > 0 & gene %in% measured_genes)
foreground <- foreground[order(
    -foreground$mean_auc, -foreground$logFC, foreground$gene
), ]
genes_of_interest <- head(foreground$gene, 20)
head(foreground[, c("gene", "logFC", "mean_auc")])
enrichment <- fishersPathwayAnalysis(
    analytes = list(genes = genes_of_interest),
    universe = list(genes = measured_genes),
    pathwayIndex = pathway_index, minPathSize = 5,
    pathwayAllInfo = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
```

Display six WikiPathways ranked by enrichment P value, each containing at
least two selected markers. Blue bars count selected pathway members;
pale bars count members in the measured background. The labels show P values
and BH-adjusted FDR from the full set of tested pathways. The dendrogram
groups pathways by shared database members using Jaccard distance.

```{r membership-workflow, message=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.8, fig.cap="Human glioma RNA: six leading WikiPathways for the selected Oligo markers, with measured-panel membership counts, enrichment P values, FDR and membership clustering."}
display <- head(subset(enrichment,
    type == "wiki" & analytes_in_pathways >= 2), 6)
visualisePathways(spe, display,
    assay = "SPT", assayName = "logcounts", minN = 2,
    pValThreshold = 1, database = database, verbose = FALSE
)
```

# Pathway network example {#worked-pathway-network}

The [human RNA/MSI example](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#pathway-network)
contains the complete code, live viewer and controls for Reactome
**Transport of small molecules** (`R-HSA-382551`). It combines measured gene
and compound effects from 240 paired tissue locations with archived interactions.

`pathwayNetworkPlots()` writes standalone HTML; `embedPathwayNetwork()` embeds
it with a **Download network HTML** button. The viewer works offline.
The returned file's `network_summary` and `pathway_coverage` attributes give
tabular summaries.

## Interaction availability

Use `verbose = TRUE` to inspect source IDs and available interactions.
The network combines recorded edges with measured pathway members.

# Inspect a pathway and its interactions

`db` holds the requested collection. `cell_cycle$protEdges` records protein
interactions, including source labels and direction. The example uses the pinned
KEGG Cell Cycle pathway `hsa:04110` to inspect the available network evidence.

```{r load-graphs, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
registry <- spaMTPDatabaseInfo(version = "3.0.7")
registry[registry$resource %in% c("ramp_kegg", "ramp_reactome",
    "ramp_wikipathway", "ramp_hmdb"), c("resource", "version", "bytes")]
db <- loadSpaMTPDatabase("ramp_kegg", version = "3.0.7")
cell_cycle <- db$ramp_kegg[["Cell cycle"]]
edges <- cell_cycle$protEdges
head(edges[, c("src", "dest", "directed", "source_reaction_type")])
```

The `r format(nrow(edges), big.mark = ",")` rows describe recorded interactions.
Repeated endpoint pairs can have distinct labels or directions. Generic
processes retain their source labels. Arrowheads mark directed interactions;
undirected interactions appear as plain edges.

## Interaction coverage

The table counts the archived interaction types, most frequent first. Counts
describe database records for this pathway; an endpoint pair can occur under
more than one interaction type.

```{r interaction-types}
sort(table(edges$source_reaction_type), decreasing = TRUE)
```

# Inspect resource provenance

The `spamtp_database` attribute records the resource version, source URL and
checksum. Save the collection with `saveRDS()` to keep these details with the
reference tables.

```{r inspect-provenance}
attr(db$ramp_kegg, "spamtp_database")[c(
    "resource", "version", "source",
    "expected_md5", "source_url"
)]
```

Continue with the [complete workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html) for paired
spatial analysis and report generation. For a worked compound network, return
to the [annotation guide](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#carry-the-annotation-threshold-into-real-pathway-analysis).
